OPEN TRIADS

Triads can also be voiced with their notes spread very far apart. These types of triads are called open triads. In an open triad, the notes span more than one octave, as opposed to the closed triads with which we began. Fig. 12 triads, both on the staff and on chord frames. Note that some of these triads are inverted as well. The E minor is in first inver- sion; the D major is in second inversion, etc.
